labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE, NOT AN EMULATED MACHINE: the maiko Lisp VM (github.com/Interlisp/medley, MIT; release medley-260826, linux x86_64 build) renders Medley's display into an X window under a pinned 1024x768 Xvfb; the daemon captures the X root (SH_CAPTURE=x11) and drives input over XTEST (SH_INPUT_BACKEND=x11test, SH_X11TEST_ABS=1: true absolute motion in root coordinates, buttons and keys as XTEST edges). No QEMU/QMP, no disk image, no exec channel — `labctl shot` reads the X root; to drive it by hand use xdotool on the station's display (only while no visitor is attached). Reset=relaunch: kill maiko by mame.pid, wipe work/, exec the release full.sysout again (~2 s to the Exec). Launcher stations/medley/x11-runtime.sh; assets in assets/medley (MANIFEST.sha256 pins the tarball).

museum.periodBrowser: none — Medley predates the web; its network was XNS/PUP to Xerox file servers, and this exhibit is not networked
museum.blurb: Xerox PARC's Lisp machine environment, the software half of the 1108 and 1186 'D-machines'. Everything on the screen is a live Lisp object: windows, menus and fonts are data you can inspect and edit while the system runs, and the structure editor edits programs as trees rather than text. Medley (1987) was the last Xerox release before Envos and then Venue took it over; the Interlisp project revived it in 2020, and this is that revival, running on the project's own portable Lisp virtual machine rather than on Xerox hardware.
museum.notes: Host-native Tier 3 with NO emulated machine: maiko (the portable Interlisp-D VM, in C since the late 1980s) is a plain X client, so the station is a stock X app under a pinned Xvfb with x11 root capture and XTEST input. Media is the pinned Interlisp release tarball (MIT; sha256 in ASSETS-MANIFEST.md) unpacked by tiles/medley.sh — no ROM, no disk, no checkpoint; reset is a ~2 s relaunch from the release full.sysout. The rest scene is the default MEDLEYDIR-INIT greet: the XCL Exec at the top-left and the Medley logo top-right. Distinct from alto/star/daybreak (Xerox's own OSes under emulation): this is the Lisp-side of the same PARC lineage, on the Interlisp project's own VM. See docs/guests/medley.md.

network.note: No network plane. maiko can bridge Lisp TCP/IP to a host TAP (its -N/nethub options) but that is a follow-up; the retronet reservation 10.99.0.39 / tap medleyrn0 is held as the uniqueness ledger only, with no tap script committed.

reset.fixture: Interlisp Medley booted from the release full.sysout with the MEDLEYDIR-INIT greet at 1024x768: white root; the black-on-white XCL 'Exec (XCL)' listener window at the top-left (+8+60, ~550x330) showing the greet transcript (a time-of-day greeting — 'Hi.' or 'Good evening.' — then the '2>' prompt); the Medley / INTERLISP / COMMON LISP logo window at the top-right; the black one-line status bar across the top (Pkg XCL-USER · Rdtbl XCL · Tty EXEC · Dir · VMem · Time). Reached ≤2 s after exec (measured 2026-09-09: f2.png == f30.png apart from the caret blink). resetMode=relaunch with no statefile: kill maiko by mame.pid, wipe work/ (LDEDESTSYSOUT lives there, so nothing a visitor SaveVM's survives), start the sysout again. The typed-in demo evaluates Common Lisp in the XCL Exec.
